messages:
jen: Heads-up: I'm hitting SSL validation errors on Windows when using the async Python SDK in a venv (py3.8). Sync client works fine.

sahil: Ugh, windows+python ssl quirks. Can you paste the traceback and what Python distro you have?

jen: Traceback snippet: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1007)
Python: CPython 3.8.16 64-bit, OpenSSL 1.1.1k  FIPS (from my company installer)
Minimal repro (async):
```python
import os, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

# I tried setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE but that didn't help
os.environ['REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE'] = r"C:\\Users\\jen\\.certs\\company-ca.pem"

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key="sk-...") as c:
        await c.generate("hi")

asyncio.run(main())
```

tkim: Thanks. Two likely things: 1) aiohttp (async path) doesn't always consult REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE on Windows due to load order, 2) our AsyncClient doesn't accept an explicit ca file or prefer certifi fallback.

sahil: Did you try SSL_CERT_FILE instead of REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE? Windows Python sometimes only respects SSL_CERT_FILE env.

jen: Tried SSL_CERT_FILE too, no dice. But when I created an explicit ssl.SSLContext(cafile=path) and injected it into the client internals, it worked. Would be great if AsyncClient exposed a simple ca_file parameter.

tkim: Agreed. We should add: AsyncClient(..., ca_file: Optional[str] = None) with fallback order: explicit -> SSL_CERT_FILE -> certifi.where(). Also unify retry behavior with the sync client (same backoff + max retries). Right now async has fewer retries for 429s.

jen: Also FYI I hit typing issues with mypy on 3.8; AsyncClient types are incomplete and some coroutine-returning helpers are typed as Any which breaks strict mypy runs in our sample app. If we add ca_file param, include proper types in the stub for py3.8 compatibility.

sahil: Can we add a tiny Windows-only integration test that sets SSL_CERT_FILE and then runs a mock server with a cert chain? Skip unless sys.platform == 'win32' to avoid flakiness. CI should run that on windows-latest for 3.8, 3.11, 3.12.

tkim: I can open a PR. Plan: minimal changes to AsyncClient __init__, add ca_file plumbing to the aiohttp connector, add RetryPolicy parity, extend types in types.pyi, and add one integration test under tests/integration/test_windows_ssl.py guarded by pytest.mark.skipif. I'll also update docs/faq.md with a short note about env var differences and recommended certifi fallback.

jen: Please also update the Python quickstart sample to show a one-liner workaround (os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE']=certifi.where()) for users who hit this before we release the client patch. That helps onboarding.

tkim: Yep. Will include sample and a migration note. I saw that some customers rely on cert bundles provided by company installers; defaulting to certifi.where() is the safest for public users while honoring explicit env or param for enterprise.

devex-bot: PR created by tkim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/459  — adds AsyncClient.ca_file, retries parity, types, and windows CI job.

sahil: Nice. Can someone with a Windows VM run the PR locally on 3.8 before merge? I can run smoke locally on 3.11.

jen: I can run 3.8 tomorrow and report back. Thanks for the quick triage.
